extracted.intended_audience: writers and critiquers using Scribophile (site members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and rules for posting works, selecting spotlights, writing critiques, earning/spending karma, and participating in the Scribophile community. Covers technical, stylistic, and procedural requirements specific to the Scribophile platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights retention when posting
rubrics_metrics.description: You keep all rights to the work you post at Scribophile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By posting you grant Scribophile the non-exclusive right to display your work (see Terms of Service, 'Use Of Content By Users'). The site exists to help you improve and does not take ownership of your work. Many members have gone on to publish work workshopped on Scribophile.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-publishing rights when posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting to a members-only critique site like Scribophile generally does not use up your 'first publishing' rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Scribophile is members-only and requires login, posting there usually won't preclude later publication. If concerned, post under a different title and delete it later, or email the publisher to ask. Use the publication showcase to see examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism risk and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is a theoretical risk of posting online, but extremely rare at Scribophile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only logged-in members can view your writing and you can limit visibility to selected members, reducing risk. No website can prevent copy-paste, so weigh the small risk against community feedback benefits. If worried, limit who sees your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karma points required to post
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have enough karma points to post a work; posting costs karma points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The karma system ensures contributors critique in exchange for posting opportunities. Earn karma by critiquing, having members react to your critiques, and writing long critiques. Both Basic and Premium members spend karma to post; Basic members are also limited to 2 posted works at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to post (technical flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post via 'Your writing' → 'Post a work for critique'; you may type in the editor or paste from a program like Word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prompts in the editor. Ensure you have sufficient karma before posting. If having editor trouble, consult the editor troubleshooting page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Spotlight: exposure and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Main Spotlight: wide exposure; work stays until you receive 3 critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pros: timely, guaranteed feedback; visibility to Scribophile public; full karma to critiquers. Cons: possible wait in line; only one work allowed in Main Spotlight at a time (you can queue others). Good for guaranteed public feedback and gaining followers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Spotlight: exposure and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Spotlight: exposure limited to your followers and groupmates; work stays until you receive 6 critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pros: no wait in line; twice as many critiques for same karma cost; easier for long-form projects and multiple simultaneous posts; can use Restricted visibility. Cons: reduced site listing visibility; you must contact followers/groupmates to get critiques; only followers/groupmates get full karma for critiquing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta Read Spotlight: exposure and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Beta Read Spotlight: for complete novels; extremely limited exposure to individuals you personally contact; work stays indefinitely until removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pros: no wait in line; no karma cost to post entire novel; work remains until you remove it. Cons: critiques earn no karma; chapters won't be visible in site listings (must share links); unlikely to get critiques from people you haven't personally contacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing a spotlight based on goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Select Main, Personal, or Beta Read spotlights depending on desired exposure, critique quantity, and whether you have arranged critiquing partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main for guaranteed public feedback; Personal when you have a network and want more critiques; Beta for arranged beta readers and no karma cost for long novels. See spotlight FAQ for details and wait time expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spotlight lifecycle and critique counting
rubrics_metrics.description: The system counts long critiques from when your work enters the Main Spotlight line; works can skip the Main Spotlight if they receive 3 long critiques while still in line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a work gets some long critiques in line and then enters spotlight, it will remain until the total required long critiques are reached. Authors can spend karma to put work back in line for more critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adult content tagging (adult checkbox)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'adult' checkbox for works with graphic sex, extreme violence, or other material likely to offend some readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule of thumb: if you can picture your grandma being OK with reading it, you probably don't need to check the box. Use the tag as a polite warning. Scribophile allows erotic/adult material but asks authors to warn readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre categorization policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres/types are intentionally kept broad to simplify categorization and searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your work doesn't have to fit perfectly; pick one or two broad categories it could be said to fit under. Avoid overly specific micro-genres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum post length for Main Spotlight
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum post length in the Main Spotlight is 4,000 words; posts longer than ~4,000 should be split.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slight leeway (e.g., 4,001 words) is acceptable, but 4,500 is too long. The 4,000-word limit is based on what the average person can critique in detail in one sitting. Personal and Beta spotlights have no length limit but still require chapter-by-chapter posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locking older works after 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: After a work leaves a spotlight, it can be critiqued/commented on for 30 more days; after 30 days it is locked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locked works are readable but not critiquable. Locking encourages attention to newer material. Authors can unlock a locked work to give it another Main Spotlight round and another 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images in posts (Premium feature and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Premium members can include images in posted works; images must be hosted externally and inserted via an image URL ending in .jpg/.png/.gif.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload to a third-party host (e.g., Postimage), copy the direct image URL, use the editor's Image button, paste the URL, and Insert. If image isn't visible, you used the wrong URL (must end in .jpg/.png/.gif).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quoting requirement in critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to offset quotations from the work you’re critiquing using the quote feature in the critique editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'quote' button or highlight text and press ctrl+o. The system ignores quoted words when calculating karma earned for a critique. Failing to quote will cause the system to count pasted text as your critique and unfairly award extra karma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline critique features and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Scribophile supports inline critiques: green boxes, strikethrough, highlights, and reaction emojis; controls differ between desktop and mobile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desktop: click to insert green box, select text to show popup for delete/highlight/emoji or use keyboard shortcuts (d, h/m). Mobile/tablet: tap to insert box; select text with touch and use Highlight or Strikethrough buttons; hide on-screen keyboard to access selection. Reaction emojis append to highlights and can be removed by tapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to write a critique (basic principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write what you as a reader thought of the work and how you would make it better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous resources are suggested (e.g., 'How to Write a Great Critique', 'But I Don’t Know How to Critique!', 'The Diplomatic Critiquer'). Focus on constructive feedback from a reader's perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karma earning rules and mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: You earn karma points for critiquing other works; longer critiques and critiques for spotlighted works earn more karma. Reactions to your critiques also earn karma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no maximum karma per critique. Critiquing spotlight works yields higher rewards. Members earn a small amount (0.01 karma) when others click reaction adjectives on their critiques; reactions also create activity feed entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction adjectives meaning and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Reactions (thorough, enlightening, encouraging, constructive, like) are ways to acknowledge good critiques and each click gives the critiquer 0.01 karma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clicking reactions increases the critique author's karma and adds to their activity feed. You can react to critiques of others to encourage good critiquing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scratchpad usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Your scratchpad is on your profile's left-hand column; you can write on other members' scratchpads but not your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short public messages can be left and replied to; location is under profile image on personal profile pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation score purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation score tracks how you stand in the community; starts at 0 and increases as people react to your critiques and posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation is a fun measure of how your activity is received relative to others and can only increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scribophile gifts (karma purchases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtual gifts can be purchased with karma points and sent to other members privately or anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gifts to thank critiquers, support favorite authors, or show appreciation; they cost karma points.

rubrics_metrics.name: How writer's groups function
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups are collections of writers with shared interests, each with forums and collections of group-submitted works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join groups to meet authors, post for group review, and participate in discussions. Groupmates can be asked to critique works (Personal Spotlight) and get full karma for doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group leader expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Group leaders are responsible for fostering engagement: moderating forums, encouraging participation, starting threads, and messaging members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active leadership is required for a group's success—doing nothing often leads to group failure. Leaders should regularly create content and remind members about activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling email delivery issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If Scribophile's emails bounce from your address (e.g., inbox full or marked spam), the delivery service cancels future delivery to that address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam folders first. If not receiving email and sure it’s not spam, contact Scribophile support to resolve bounced mail issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocking and reporting problematic members
rubrics_metrics.description: You can block members to prevent them from contacting you or reading/critiquing your work; report abusive behavior to admins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block via a member's profile page. For disrespectful, abusive, or inappropriate behavior, contact admins so they can address it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest listing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: To get a writing contest listed in Scribophile's contests section, check the site requirements and contact staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed requirements and get in touch with Scribophile to request listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile picture 'safe for work' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile pictures must be 'safe for work' (SFW): appropriate for public/workplace settings and not likely to offend passersby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SFW generally means no extreme violence/gore and no overt sexual content or nudity. The definition is subjective and staff reserve the right to make case-by-case judgments. Rationale: unlike posted writing, profile pictures are displayed without content warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upgrading to Premium and feature differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Premium membership grants additional features (e.g., image inclusion, unlimited posted works, no ads); Basic has limitations (2 posted works).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can upgrade, gift upgrades, or change subscription type (cancel current then re-upgrade). Premium members should not see ads; if they do, check for adware. Some behaviors (e.g., posting images) are restricted to Premium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pen name change policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pen name can be changed only if you have reputation under 100, the new pen name sounds like a real name, and you haven't changed pen names before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No exceptions are granted. Contact support only if you meet those conditions; don't expect an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ad appearance for Premium members indicates malware
rubrics_metrics.description: Premium members should not see ads; sudden ad display likely indicates adware/spyware on the user's device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check browser addons/extensions for suspicious items, disable them one by one, scan installed programs, or contact a repair professional if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription changes and cancellation behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancel monthly subscription to switch to yearly; after cancelation your account remains upgraded through the last paid term and then downgrades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account data and posts are retained; upon downgrade, Basic membership limitations apply (e.g., posted-work limits). Price is locked for the life of a subscription; canceling and re-upgrading later may require paying current prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of downgrade on posted work and messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Downgrading to Basic does not delete posts/data, but Basic limits apply immediately after downgrade (e.g., must delete works to go under the Basic posted-work limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if you have more than the Basic limit of posts or too many messages, you'll need to delete items before you can post/send more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulk message deletion limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is currently no way to delete multiple inbox messages at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must delete messages individually for now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password reset and lost email limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: You can reset your password using the password reset page by entering the email address you signed up with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you've also forgotten the email address or lost access to it, Scribophile has limited ability to help.
